title: Finite-sum bilevel optimization: a lower bound under linear-iteration restrictions.
summary: Solve the bilevel problem $\min_x\Phi(x)$, where $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$ and $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ is the unique global lower-level solution. The upper- and lower-level variables are $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$. Seek approximate stationarity of the reduced objective under the stated error criterion and guarantee. Assumptions on $f$, $g$, and $\Phi$ are specified separately. Here $f=n_f^{-1}\sum_if_i$ and $g=n_g^{-1}\sum_jg_j$.

task.detail: f=(1/n_f) sum_i f_i, g=(1/n_g) sum_j g_j; Phi(x)=f(x,y*(x)); y* is the unique global lower minimizer.
description_paragraphs: Solve the bilevel problem $\min_x\Phi(x)$, where $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$ and $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ is the unique global lower-level solution. The upper- and lower-level variables are $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$. Seek approximate stationarity of the reduced objective under the stated error criterion and guarantee. Assumptions on $f$, $g$, and $\Phi$ are specified separately. Here $f=n_f^{-1}\sum_if_i$ and $g=n_g^{-1}\sum_jg_j$.

model.function_class: Each f_i has an L_F-Lipschitz gradient. Each g_j is twice continuously differentiable and mu_y-strongly convex in y. There is no additional uniform value-Lipschitz, Hessian-Lipschitz or third-derivative budget in Definition 4.1.
model.initialization: Public x0,y0,v0; Phi(x0)-inf Phi<=Delta. No uniform lower initial-distance or v-distance budget is asserted for this native lower-bound class.
model.geometry: Phi may be nonconvex; all vector norms are Euclidean.
description_paragraphs: Each $f_i$ has $L_F$-Lipschitz joint gradient. Each $g_j$ is twice continuously differentiable and $\mu_y$-strongly convex in $y$. This lower-bound class imposes no additional uniform Lipschitz budgets on function values, Hessians, or third derivatives.
The points $x_0,y_0,v_0$ are public and $\Phi(x_0)-\inf\Phi\le\Delta$. No additional bound is imposed on the initial inner or adjoint distance.
model.outer_geometry: The reduced objective may be nonconvex. Its differentiability or local Lipschitz regularity is specified by the model and accuracy measure.

operations: Choose i in [n_f], j in [n_g], (x,y,v); receive the exact tuple (grad f_i(x,y), grad g_j(x,y), g_{j,yy}(x,y)v, g_{j,xy}(x,y)v).
oracle.query_domain: Whole Euclidean space, subject to the linear-algorithm transcript restrictions below.
oracle.coupling: Components can be revisited; no stochastic sample noise.
description_paragraphs: A query selects $i,j,x,y,v$ and returns the exact joint response $(\nabla f_i,\nabla g_j,g_{j,yy}v,g_{j,xy}v)$, with every component evaluated at $(x,y)$. Components may be queried repeatedly.
Return an outer point from the restricted iteration sequence. An arbitrary terminal output outside the permitted span cannot enlarge the algorithm class.
